land.text: all of County Cork and most of County Kerry
'Following the Nine Years' War of the 1590s, Desmond became part of the Kingdom of Ireland'; partitioned between County Cork and County Kerry in 1606

successors.note: Carbery, Muskerry and Duhallow were MacCarthy principalities inside it.

capitals.name: Killarney
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Killarney, Lough Leane and Cahersiveen'; the page gives no years.

correction.text: 'all of what is now County Cork and most of County Kerry'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has no Kingdom of Desmond (its Earldom of Desmond row is the Anglo-Norman earldom, 1333-1458). No area on the page. Waterford and Limerick are not named.

correction.text: the western half: 'the eastern half of Desmond was conquered by the Anglo-Normans' and became the Earldom of Desmond

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the page gives no year for the Norman conquest of the eastern half ('the late 12th century'); 1177 is the year the Council of Oxford granted Desmond to FitzStephen and de Cogan (Norman invasion article). The 60 km radius round Cork is the researcher's reading of 'eastern half'. The Battle of Callann (1261) 'helped preserve Desmond's independence'.

ledger.note: 1118: Tadhg Mac Carthaigh founds the Kingdom of Desmond. 'It was founded in 1118 by Tadhg Mac Carthaigh, King of Munster'; the Treaty of Glanmire 'formally divided the Kingdom of Munster into Desmond and Thomond'.

region.text: the eastern half of Desmond, granted at the Council of Oxford to Robert FitzStephen and Miles de Cogan

ledger.note: 1177: Henry II grants Desmond to FitzStephen and de Cogan. 'granted Desmond to Robert FitzStephen and Miles de Cogan'. The Desmond page says only that 'the eastern half of Desmond was conquered by the Anglo-Normans' in 'the late 12th century' and that it 'became the Earldom of Desmond, ruled by the Fitzmaurices and FitzGeralds'.

region.text: the western half, ruled by the MacCarthy Mor

ledger.note: 1596: the last MacCarthy Mor king dies and Desmond becomes part of the Kingdom of Ireland. Infobox 'Disestablished: 1596'; 'After the death of King Donal IX MacCarthy Mor in 1596'; 'The MacCarthy Mor family ruled ... From its inception in 1118 through 1596'.

wars.name: Battle of Callann
wars.outcome: MacCarthy victory over the Anglo-Normans, which 'helped preserve Desmond's independence'.
wars.note: The page dates only the battle.

wars.name: Desmond Rebellions
wars.outcome: Fought by the Earls of Desmond, not the MacCarthy kings; recorded in the Kingdom of Ireland dossier.
wars.note: Listed so the reviewer can see it was considered; the Desmond page does not cover it.

certainty.note: The frontier with the Earldom is unmarked on the page.

sources.title: Kingdom of Desmond
sources.note: Identity, 1118, 1596, extent, Norman conquest of the east.

notes: Cliopatria's Earldom of Desmond (1333-1458) and the earldom-of-desmond dossier (1329-1583) are the Anglo-Norman eastern half; that dossier gives kingdom-of-england as predecessor, but the legal predecessor is the Lordship of Ireland. The MacCarthy sub-kingdoms (Carbery from the mid-13th century, Muskerry from the 14th) are 'principalities' inside this state and have no dossier. The Cork radius for the eastern half is a bridge.
